cards.back: A rock formed when magma or lava cools and solidifies
A rock formed from compacted and cemented sediment
A rock changed by heat and pressure without melting
A coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock rich in quartz and feldspar
A fine-grained extrusive igneous rock that forms oceanic crust
A sedimentary rock made mainly of calcite, often from shells
A sedimentary rock made of cemented sand grains
A metamorphic rock formed from limestone
A fine-grained metamorphic rock formed from shale
The continuous change of rocks between igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic forms
The process that turns loose sediment into solid rock
Parallel layering in metamorphic rock caused by pressure
A naturally occurring inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and crystal structure
A scale of mineral hardness from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond)
A hard mineral made of silicon dioxide that scratches glass

cards.front: What is cleavage in a mineral?
cards.back: The way a mineral splits along flat planes of weakness
How the surface of a mineral reflects light, such as metallic or glassy
The most abundant group of minerals in the Earth's crust
A mineral of calcium carbonate that fizzes in dilute acid
The theory that the lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the asthenosphere

cards.front: What happens at a divergent boundary?
cards.back: Plates move apart and new crust forms, as at a mid-ocean ridge

cards.front: What happens at a convergent boundary?
cards.back: Plates collide, producing mountains, trenches and volcanoes
One plate sinking beneath another into the mantle
Plates slide past each other, as on the San Andreas Fault
A fracture in rock along which movement has occurred
Sudden release of stored strain along a fault

cards.front: What does the Richter scale measure?
cards.back: The magnitude of an earthquake from the seismic waves it produces

cards.front: What are P waves and S waves?
cards.back: P waves are compressional and fastest, S waves are shear waves that cannot pass through liquid

cards.front: What is the focus of an earthquake?
cards.back: The point underground where the rock first breaks
An opening in the crust where magma, ash and gas escape
A plume of hot mantle rising under a plate, such as under Hawaii
Wegener's idea that the continents have moved across the Earth
The preserved remains or traces of an organism from the past

cards.front: What is the principle of superposition?
cards.back: In undisturbed layers the oldest rock is at the bottom
Using the decay of radioactive isotopes to find the age of a rock
The time taken for half of the atoms of a radioactive isotope to decay
A fossil of a species that lived briefly and widely, used to date rock layers
A gap in the rock record where erosion or no deposition occurred
A rapid diversification of animal life about 540 million years ago

cards.front: What caused the extinction of the dinosaurs?
cards.back: An asteroid impact about 66 million years ago
The breakdown of rock at the Earth's surface by water, ice, wind and chemicals
The removal and transport of weathered material
The laying down of sediment when the transporting agent loses energy
